guideTitle: The Best Single Monitor Arms, From $20 Clamps to Ergotron
metaTitle: Best Single Monitor Arms: Budget, Premium and Heavy-Duty (2026)
metaDescription: We compared single monitor arms on weight range, screen size, curved-monitor support, mounting options and spring mechanism, from budget HUANUO and ErGear arms to Ergotron.
introParagraphs: A single monitor arm is easy to buy wrong in two ways: choosing on screen size when weight is what matters, and ignoring the lower end of the weight range. A gas-spring arm is tuned for a band of weights; a monitor below it may drift upward, and one near the top may sag.

So start with your monitor's weight without its stand (in its specification sheet), its VESA pattern, and whether it is curved. Then check that your desk edge suits a clamp or has a grommet hole. After that, the choice is between budget arms that cover standard flat monitors, Ergotron arms rated for curved and ultrawide screens, and a heavy-duty HUANUO for large panels.

Our comparison is based on published specifications, including weight and size ranges, VESA support and mounting options, plus price position, not hands-on testing. Prices range from about $20 to $199 at the time of writing.

huanuo-flowlift-single-monitor-arm.summary: A full-motion arm for 13- to 32-inch monitors from 4.4 to 19.8 lb, with clamp or grommet mounting.
huanuo-flowlift-single-monitor-arm.description:
The HUANUO FlowLift is the sensible default for a standard flat monitor: it fits 13- to 32-inch screens weighing 4.4 to 19.8 lb, with full-motion tilt, swivel and rotation, and a base that clamps or mounts through a grommet hole.

That weight band covers many office monitors. It is widely reviewed and costs about $33 at the time of writing.

It is not rated for curved or ultrawide monitors. At the time of writing the FlowLift Pro costs slightly less and lists a smoother spring mechanism, so compare both prices before ordering.
cons: Not rated for curved or ultrawide monitors
Very light monitors may fall below the 4.4 lb minimum
huanuo-flowlift-single-monitor-arm.bestFor: Standard flat monitors on a typical desk.
huanuo-flowlift-single-monitor-arm.skipIf: The FlowLift Pro is cheaper when you buy; it adds a smoother mechanism.

huanuo-flowlift-pro-single-monitor-arm.summary: HUANUO's MechaSpring mechanism and a tool-free VESA head, for 13- to 32-inch monitors up to 19.8 lb.
huanuo-flowlift-pro-single-monitor-arm.description:
The FlowLift Pro is the pick for anyone who moves the monitor often, such as standing desk users: HUANUO says its MechaSpring mechanism gives smoother, more even resistance through the range of motion.

It fits 13- to 32-inch monitors up to 19.8 lb, has a tool-free VESA head and mounts by clamp or grommet. At the time of writing it costs slightly less than the standard FlowLift.

It has the same 19.8 lb ceiling and is not rated for curved or ultrawide monitors.
cons: Not rated for curved or ultrawide monitors
huanuo-flowlift-pro-single-monitor-arm.bestFor: Standing desks and anyone who repositions the monitor daily.
huanuo-flowlift-pro-single-monitor-arm.skipIf: Your monitor is curved or heavy; look at the Ergotron LX or HUANUO TitanLift.

ergear-single-monitor-arm.summary: A tool-free arm for 13- to 34-inch monitors up to 19.8 lb, with cable management, for about $20.
ergear-single-monitor-arm.description:
The ErGear is the low-cost choice for a modest setup: it fits 13- to 34-inch monitors up to 19.8 lb on a VESA 100 x 100mm head, with tool-free installation and a built-in cable channel.

It is a reasonable first monitor arm for a standard flat screen.

The listing does not mention a tension adjustment, and budget clamp hardware should not be overtightened on a thin or hollow-core desk.
ergear-single-monitor-arm.bestFor: Budget buyers with a standard flat monitor.
ergear-single-monitor-arm.skipIf: Your monitor weighs over 20 lb; the WALI is rated for 26.4 lb at the same price.

wali-single-monitor-mount.badge: Best Budget Arm for Heavier Monitors
wali-single-monitor-mount.summary: A budget arm with a 26.4 lb rating for screens up to 32 inches.
wali-single-monitor-mount.description:
The WALI is the budget arm with the most weight headroom: WALI rates it for regular screens up to 32 inches and 26.4 lb, noticeably more than the ErGear or FlowLift at a similar price.

That margin is useful for a heavier 32-inch monitor that would sit near the limit of a 19.8 lb arm. It uses VESA 75 or 100mm.

Cable management is minimal, the listing does not mention a grommet option, and it is not rated for curved or ultrawide panels.
wali-single-monitor-mount.bestFor: Heavier flat 32-inch monitors on a budget.
wali-single-monitor-mount.skipIf: Your monitor is curved; the Ergotron LX is rated for curved panels.

nb-smoovex-monitor-mount.summary: A mechanical-spring arm with a compact base for monitors up to 32 inches.
nb-smoovex-monitor-mount.description:
The NB SmooVex is the pick for a small desk: a compact base that takes little surface, with a mechanical spring mount for monitors up to 32 inches on VESA 75 or 100mm.

It is a straightforward arm without extras.

The listing does not state a weight rating clearly, so check your monitor's weight against NB's specifications before ordering. It is not rated for curved monitors.
nb-smoovex-monitor-mount.bestFor: Small desks where a bulky clamp would take too much space.
nb-smoovex-monitor-mount.skipIf: You need a stated weight rating; the WALI or FlowLift list theirs.

ergotron-lx-monitor-arm-single.summary: Ergotron's LX for flat, curved and ultrawide monitors up to 34 inches, 7 to 25 lb.
ergotron-lx-monitor-arm-single.description:
The Ergotron LX is the premium choice, and one of only three arms here suited to curved or ultrawide monitors: Ergotron rates it for flat, curved and ultrawide screens up to 34 inches, weighing 7 to 25 lb.

Its gas-spring arm has a tension adjustment at the joint, which lets you rebalance it for a different monitor or if it starts to sag. It supports VESA 75 and 100mm.

It costs several times as much as the budget arms at the time of writing, and its 7 lb minimum may be too high for very light monitors. Ergotron's warranty covers defects, not normal wear.
specs: Screen size: up to 34" (flat, curved, ultrawide)
ergotron-lx-monitor-arm-single.bestFor: Curved or ultrawide monitors up to 34 inches.
ergotron-lx-monitor-arm-single.skipIf: Your monitor is flat and under 20 lb; a HUANUO arm costs far less.

ergotron-lx-pro-monitor-arm-single.badge: Best Premium Arm for Lighter Curved Monitors
ergotron-lx-pro-monitor-arm-single.summary: The upgraded LX Pro in white, rated for 4 to 22 lb and screens up to 34 inches.
ergotron-lx-pro-monitor-arm-single.description:
The Ergotron LX Pro is the upgraded LX, with a refined joint design and a white finish. It covers flat, curved and ultrawide monitors up to 34 inches, weighing 4 to 22 lb.

The lower 4 lb minimum suits lighter monitors that fall below the standard LX's 7 lb floor. It keeps the VESA 75 and 100mm support and tension adjustment.

It is the most expensive arm here at the time of writing, and its 22 lb ceiling is lower than the LX's 25 lb.
specs: Screen size: up to 34" (flat, curved, ultrawide)
ergotron-lx-pro-monitor-arm-single.bestFor: Lighter curved or ultrawide monitors, or a white desk setup.
ergotron-lx-pro-monitor-arm-single.skipIf: Your monitor weighs over 22 lb; the standard LX goes to 25 lb.

huanuo-titanlift-heavy-duty-arm-single.badge: Best for Heavy and Large Monitors
huanuo-titanlift-heavy-duty-arm-single.summary: A heavy-duty aluminum arm for screens up to 49 inches and 44 lb.
huanuo-titanlift-heavy-duty-arm-single.description:
The HUANUO TitanLift is the arm for heavy panels: HUANUO rates it for screens up to 49 inches and 44 lb, far above any other arm here, with aluminum construction and a dual C-clamp base.

It suits large ultrawides and heavy monitors that exceed the Ergotron arms' ratings, and it costs about half as much as an Ergotron at the time of writing.

Its VESA head tops out at 100 x 100mm, so check your monitor's pattern, and it needs a desk edge the dual clamp can grip.
pros: Costs less than the Ergotron arms
huanuo-titanlift-heavy-duty-arm-single.bestFor: Heavy or very large monitors, including 49-inch ultrawides.
huanuo-titanlift-heavy-duty-arm-single.skipIf: Your monitor is light; a heavy-duty arm may not balance well at the low end, and a FlowLift costs far less.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Find your monitor's weight without its stand in its specification sheet, and choose an arm whose range puts it comfortably inside, not at either end. Ranges here run from 4 lb (LX Pro minimum) to 44 lb (TitanLift maximum).
Curved monitors sit further forward on the mount. The Ergotron LX and LX Pro are rated for curved and ultrawide screens up to 34 inches; the TitanLift for screens up to 49 inches.
Most arms here support 75 or 100mm patterns. Check your monitor's pattern, especially on large ultrawides.
Clamps need a solid desk edge; grommet mounts need a hole. Glass, hollow-core or very thin desks may need reinforcement or a different solution.
An adjustable spring lets you rebalance the arm if the monitor drifts or sags. The Ergotron arms list it; check the budget listings.

faq.q: Why does my monitor arm slowly droop?
faq.a: The spring may be set too light for the monitor, or may have lost some tension over time. If the arm has a tension adjustment, as the Ergotron arms do, tighten it. If not, and the monitor is near the arm's maximum, a higher-rated arm may be needed.

faq.q: How much reach do I need?
faq.a: Enough to bring the screen to a comfortable viewing distance from where you sit, and to push it back when needed. Compare the arm's listed reach with your desk depth and seating position.

faq.q: Will my monitor arm wobble when I type?
faq.a: Some movement is normal on most arms, especially if the desk itself flexes. A sturdier arm and a solid, stable desk reduce it.

faq.q: Can I mount a curved monitor on these arms?
faq.a: The Ergotron LX and LX Pro are rated for curved and ultrawide screens up to 34 inches, and the HUANUO TitanLift for screens up to 49 inches. The budget arms here are not listed for curved monitors.

faq.q: Do I need a different arm for a standing desk?
faq.a: Not necessarily, but an arm that adjusts easily helps if you move the screen often. The FlowLift Pro's mechanism is designed for smoother adjustment.

faq.q: Does a long warranty mean the arm won't sag?
faq.a: No. Warranties generally cover manufacturing defects, not normal wear. A tension adjustment is the more practical safeguard.

bottomLine: For a standard flat monitor, a HUANUO FlowLift is the sensible default; buy whichever of the FlowLift and FlowLift Pro is cheaper when you order. The ErGear is the lowest-cost option, the WALI adds capacity for heavier 32-inch screens, and the NB SmooVex suits small desks.

For a curved or ultrawide monitor up to 34 inches, the Ergotron LX is worth paying more for, and the LX Pro suits lighter screens. For heavy panels or 49-inch ultrawides, the HUANUO TitanLift offers the most capacity for about half the Ergotron price.
